Cc: procurement@novahealth.com

Subject: MSA / Order Form redlines — DPA questions and EU transfer fallback

Hi Avery / Ben,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached are Nova Health's redlines to the MSA and the proposed DPA (see NovaHealth_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx). Our legal team has two items we'd like to confirm before we can move to signatures:

1) SCCs + Transfer Impact Addendum: we redlined language asking for a Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA) referencing the SCCs and a statement about any onshore fallback.
2) EU-only processing guarantee: we asked for a short-term EU-only processing guarantee or the option for a Private deployment (VPC) for the production tenant while we finish procurement.

Can Redwood confirm whether you can: accept the TIA as drafted (we included sample wording), and provide a 60–90 day EU-only processing commitment (operational gating or an SLA-backed routing policy)? If not, please flag the constraints and any alternate mitigations (e.g., UK extension + documented subprocessors + additional audit evidence).

We'd like to close legal within two weeks if possible. I've copied procurement to keep timelines aligned.

Attachments: NovaHealth_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx, OrderForm_Redline_20270228.pdf

Thanks — Natalie
Natalie Ross

Ben — this is in the RDW pipeline (deal RDW-78321) and procurement is pushing for a two-week turnaround.

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Natalie Ross <natalie.ross@novahealth.com>, procurement@novahealth.com
Date: 2027-02-28T13:37:00-08:00
Subject: RE: MSA / Order Form redlines — DPA questions and EU transfer fallback

Thanks — I reviewed Nova's DPA redlines and the TIA language. High-level position and recommended edits below (summary for commercial):

1) Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA):
- Accept in principle but replace any absolute wording that implies we guarantee no transfers outside the EEA. We can commit to routing preferences and documented subprocessors, and to providing the TIA with a statement of technical/organizational safeguards and subprocessors.
- Add a short clause that permits fallback routing (to alternate regions) for operational continuity with prior notice and a remediation window — this protects availability during outages.

2) EU-only processing guarantee / Private deployment request:
- EU-only processing for a fixed onboarding window (60–90 days) is reasonable as a temporary, operationally-controlled routing policy. We should avoid long-term contractual commitments that require dedicated on-prem or reserved Private deployment unless Customer pays for Dedicated/Private. Proposed redline: 90-day EU-only routing commitment; ops to confirm feasibility and costs for Private deployment as a separate line item.

3) Audit rights & subprocessor notice:
- Narrow audit scope to on-site or remote audit with reasonable notice; provide SOC 2 + written subprocessor roster + commit to 30-day notice for material subprocessor changes.

4) Liability/Indemnity flags:
- Their redlines include expanded liability for data incidents. We'll push back to keep indemnity tied to Redwood's proven breach obligations and exclude consequential damages to the extent permitted by law.

Next steps for commercial/ops:
- Laura / Ops: confirm whether routing policy change (EU pinning) can be implemented as a tenancy routing flag and whether any orchestration or billing impacts exist.
- Ben / Sales: confirm whether Customer is OK with a 90-day operational guarantee and separate pricing for Private/Dedicated if requested.

If Ops confirms feasibility, I'll prepare a tracked redline with the language above and send back to Nova. Target: send legal redline by EOD 2027-03-01.

Attachments: redlines_legal_comments.docx

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Avery / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and for outlining next steps. We appreciate the willingness to accept a TIA with the caveats you described. Two asks from procurement side before we move to DocuSign:

1) Please send the final redlined DPA (tracked) incorporating the TIA language + the 90-day EU processing commitment as discussed.
2) Share a DocuSign envelope when you're ready. We will aim to get internal approvals within two weeks once the final redline is received.

If you need a formal purchase order or SOW for Private/Dedicated pricing, flag that as a separate procurement line item.

Thanks —
